What a callback is handed: which element it is about, what happened to it, and the context it lives in.

One name is one function, and that function hears about everything that happens to the element: the three mouse buttons, an INPUT from a press or from enter or space on a focused button, a HOVER as the cursor comes onto it, and a DRAG while a draggable one is moved. A function that acts on all of them would fire when the cursor merely arrived, so anything that only wants a press asks `isPress`.

Nothing is told about a release, a wheel, a key other than enter and space, or an element being scrolled, and HOVER is only told about the way in, never the way out.

```java
import net.tutla.craftytml.client.dom.CTMLCallback;
```

### `public boolean isPress()`

Whether this is the element being operated: a press on a button, or a left click on anything else. One name is one function, and that function hears about everything that happens to the element, the cursor merely arriving over it among them, so anything that only wants to be told about a press has to say so. This is how it says it.
